stem: The figure shows a 6 V cell, two identical lamps P and Q on separate branches, and two switches, S1 and S2. Both switches are closed and both lamps are lit. Switch S1 is then opened. What happens to the lamps?
options: Both P and Q go out.
Both lamps stay lit but become dimmer.
working: S1 is in the main part of the circuit, next to the cell: every path from the cell passes through it.
Opening S1 breaks the only route back to the cell, so no current flows in either branch.
Both lamps go out. (Opening S2 instead would switch off only Q, because S2 is in Q's branch.)

distractors.1: No switch sits on P's branch alone. S1 is in the main circuit, not on a branch.
distractors.2: That is what opening S2 would do: S2 is on Q's branch only.
distractors.4: A lamp dims only if the potential difference across it falls. Here the current stops completely.

hints: Put your finger on the cell and trace the loop through lamp P. Does your finger pass S1?
Now trace the loop through lamp Q. A switch that every loop passes through controls every lamp.
notes: Demo path item, drafted by Claude Code; reuses the pack's original circuit figure. Founder review pending.

stem: The bar chart shows the power ratings of five appliances in a flat. The kettle is used for 15 minutes every day for 30 days. Electricity costs $0.30 per kWh. How much does it cost to use the kettle for the 30 days?
working: From the chart, the kettle's power rating is 2000 W = 2 kW.
Time: 15 min = 0.25 h a day, so 0.25 h × 30 days = 7.5 h.

distractors.1: That is the cost for one day only (0.5 kWh × $0.30). The question asks for 30 days.
distractors.3: Used 15 hours instead of 15 minutes. Change minutes to hours first.
distractors.4: Used 2000 W instead of 2 kW, so the answer is 1000 times too big.

hints: Two conversions come before any multiplying: watts to kilowatts, and minutes to hours.
Energy in kWh = power in kW × time in hours for all 30 days. Then multiply by the price of one kWh.

stem: The figure shows a 6 V cell, a variable resistor R, a lamp L and an ammeter in one loop. The resistance of R is decreased. Which statement correctly describes AND explains what happens to lamp L?
options: L becomes brighter, because the resistance of the circuit decreases, so a larger current flows.
L becomes dimmer, because more of the current is used up by R.
L stays the same, because the voltage of the cell has not changed.
L becomes brighter, because R now gives more energy to the current.
working: R, L and the ammeter are in one series loop.
Decreasing R decreases the effective resistance of the circuit.
For the same 6 V supply, a lower resistance means a larger current flows through every part of the loop, including L.
A larger current through L makes it brighter, and the ammeter reading increases.

distractors.2: Current is not used up. And less resistance means more current, not less.
distractors.3: The supply is the same, but the resistance changed, so the current changes too.
distractors.4: Right effect, wrong reason. A resistor does not give energy; lower resistance lets a larger current flow.

hints: Say the chain out loud: resistance down → current … → lamp …
R and L are in the same loop, so whatever happens to the current through R also happens through L.
notes: Demo path item, drafted by Claude Code; reuses the pack's original circuit figure. Founder review pending.
